newsitem.title: INDIA: Fully convertible India rupee recommended in 3 yrs.
newsitem.headline: Fully convertible India rupee recommended in 3 yrs.

text.p: The Indian rupee should be prepared for full convertiblity in the next three years, a panel charged with plotting the path toward freeing the exchange rate recommended in a report presented to the Reserve Bank of India on Tuesday.
:Fully convertible India rupee recommended in 3 yrs

The report, commissioned by Finance Minister P. Chidambaram in his budget statement on February 28, said India needed to achieve 3-5 percent annual inflation over the next three years and reduce its fiscal deficit to 3.5 percent of GDP as preconditions for convertibility.

The report favoured full deregulation of interest rates in 1997 and 1998, and called for the RBI to lower banks cash reserve ratio (CRR) to 3.0 percent by 1999/2000 as another precondition for convertibility.
The panel also called for a minimum net foreign assets to currency ratio of 40 percent before convertibility was achieved.

It said Indians should be allowed to invest in global financial markets and banks and financial institutions allowed to trade in domestic and foreign gold markets. And it urged a phased liberalisation of controls on Indian capital outflows.
